sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: In vivo and ex vivo characterization of the knock-in mice was performed; the receptor is functional in the endogenous context (implied by use as a physiological tool), though specific functional assay metrics are not quoted in the clip.
sites.rationale: GPR39 topology begins extracellular at residue 1 with no signal peptide, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepended tag. The knock-in is at the endogenous locus in a full-length receptor context, ruling out a truncated or secreted construct. No residue number is named in the clip, so the junction is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=0 (before M1). The 30-residue N-terminal extracellular domain provides ample clearance from TM1 (which begins at residue 31). CRISPR/EGE knock-in of an HA tag into the endogenous mouse Gpr39 locus, producing a full-length, membrane-anchored receptor used for in vivo and ex vivo characterization. No residue number is stated in the clip. GPR39 has no signal peptide (topology string begins O at residue 1), so the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus; the tag must prepend before M1.

sources.claim: GPR39-HA knock-in mice ( Gpr39 HA ) and GPR39 knockout mice ( Gpr39 KO or Gpr39 −/− ) were created with CRISPR/EGE platform in the C57BL/6 strain by Beijing Biocytogen.
For membrane expression of mutants, a 3× HA tag at the N-terminus was added.

literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1 and L2) converge on the same physical junction (N-terminal prepend, insert_after_residue=0) because GPR39 is a GPCR with no signal peptide and a 30-residue extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 1–30) preceding TM1 at residue 31. L1 provides higher validation (endogenous knock-in, in vivo use) while L2 provides the more explicit positional statement ('N-terminus'). No ledger line grounds any insertion in ECL1 (92–109), ECL2 (173–222), or ECL3 (305–323), so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminus (residues 347–453) is intracellular and is not supported by any ledger line for a surface tag.
